patients.summary: Dental hygienist with treated Hodgkin lymphoma (2014) and hypertension who joins in 2022, is found to have HER2-positive right breast cancer in 2024 and goes through lumpectomy, chemotherapy with trastuzumab, radiation and tamoxifen. Trastuzumab is stopped for an asymptomatic LVEF drop; tamoxifen brings endometrial hyperplasia, an IUD and an AGC Pap with Actinomyces. Hyperlipidemia is never treated.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller wants to transfer care here; her previous primary care doctor retired over the summer. Reviewed membership and how insurance still applies to labs and imaging. New patient visit set for 9/13 at 8:40. Release signed electronically for prior office records; request sent. Asked her to bring her blood pressure medicines or a list.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every morning

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
45 y/o woman, dental hygienist, transferring care after her prior PCP retired.

HTN: diagnosed some years back at her old office. Takes HCTZ 25 every morning and lisinopril 10 daily, rarely misses. Checks BP at work now and then, usually 120s/80ish. No headaches, chest pain or swelling.

Oncologic hx: Hodgkin lymphoma in 2014, treated with combination chemo plus radiation at an academic center, in remission since. Discharged from oncology follow-up a couple of years ago. Has her treatment summary somewhere at home, will look.

PSH: none. Meds as above. NKDA.
FH: mother has HTN and osteoporosis (broke a hip at 70) and had uterine (endometrial) cancer at 60. Father had coronary disease young, at 55. Maternal aunt had breast cancer at 52.
SH: never smoked, no alcohol. Hygienist in a group dental office, 4 days a week.
Gyn: periods regular. Last Pap and mammogram at prior office last year, normal per pt; records requested.

Exam: BP and vitals as recorded. Well appearing. Thyroid without nodules. No cervical, supraclavicular or axillary nodes. Heart RRR no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd benign. No edema.

A/P
1. Essential HTN, controlled on HCTZ 25 + lisinopril 10. Continue. CMP today.
2. Hx Hodgkin lymphoma in remission. CBC, TSH today. Will get her treatment summary for the chart.
3. Health maintenance: lipids, hep C and HIV screen (done once, she agrees). Tdap given today (none she can recall). Screening mammogram due next month, order placed. Colonoscopy at 45 - discussed, she'd like to wait till spring.
4. Return in 6 months for BP, sooner if needed.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Gretchen, your labs look good: kidney function, potassium, blood count and thyroid are all normal, and the hepatitis C and HIV screens are negative. LDL cholesterol is a bit above ideal; nothing to start for it, we'll recheck it next year. Take care.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: MA
documents.body: 11 pages from prior PCP office scanned. Contents: visit notes 2019-2022 for hypertension on hydrochlorothiazide and lisinopril; Pap 2021 negative for intraepithelial lesion; screening mammogram 2021 BI-RADS 1, negative; lymphoma treatment summary not included. Allergies listed as NKDA. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Outside records reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed. BP control has been steady on this regimen for years. Pap and mammogram current. Lymphoma treatment summary not in this packet; pt says she'll forward hers.

reports.text: Bilateral screening mammogram with tomosynthesis. Comparison with outside study from 2021. Breasts are heterogeneously dense, which may obscure small masses. No suspicious mass, architectural distortion or suspicious calcifications in either breast. Skin and nipples unremarkable.

documents.title: Vaccine visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Came after work for vaccines. Afebrile, no acute illness. Flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM left deltoid; Pfizer bivalent booster IM right deltoid. VIS provided. Observed 15 minutes, no reaction. Mammogram result reviewed with her; she had already seen it in the portal.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Hypertension Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Here for BP. Feels well. Taking both meds. Work busy - short-staffed, more patients per day. No dizziness on standing, no cramps.
O: Vitals reviewed, BP at goal. Heart regular. Lungs clear. No ankle edema.
A/P: HTN controlled on HCTZ 25 / lisinopril 10. BMP today for K and creatinine on the diuretic and ACE inhibitor. Colonoscopy referral sent today now that she's ready. Physical in the fall.

documents.title: Colonoscopy report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body: Outpatient endoscopy unit. Procedure date 6/23/2023. Indication: screening, average risk, first exam. Prep: good, adequate in all segments. Cecum reached and identified by appendiceal orifice and ileocecal valve. Withdrawal time 9 minutes. Findings: normal mucosa throughout the colon and rectum; no polyps; small internal hemorrhoids on retroflexion. Impression: normal screening colonoscopy. Recommendation: next screening colonoscopy in 10 years. Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
46F annual.

Interval: colonoscopy in June was normal, 10-yr recall. No new issues. BP fine at home checks. Walks most evenings.

ROS negative incl. no breast changes, no fevers or sweats, no weight loss, no new lumps anywhere.
Meds: HCTZ 25, lisinopril 10. NKDA.
PHQ-2 0.

Exam: vitals as charted. HEENT normal. Thyroid normal. No lymphadenopathy cervical/supraclavicular/axillary. Breasts deferred to mammogram per her preference; no concerns reported. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Skin no lesions of concern. Ext no edema.

A/P
- HTN: at goal. Continue. CMP.
- Hx Hodgkin lymphoma 2014: remains well.
- Lipids repeat today (LDL was borderline last year).
- Mammogram due next month - ordered. Pap current (2021), next due 2024.
- Flu and updated COVID given.
- Follow up in 6 months.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs from your physical are back. Kidneys, liver and potassium are normal. LDL cholesterol is about where it was last year, borderline. Keep up the walking. See you in the spring.

reports.text: Bilateral screening mammogram with tomosynthesis, compared with 10/2022. Heterogeneously dense breast tissue. No new or suspicious mass, distortion or grouped calcifications. Stable bilateral appearance.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fax: 90-day refills requested for hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg and lisinopril 10 mg. Last BMP 3/2023 normal, seen 9/2023. Sent per protocol, 90 days x 1 refill each.
